transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I’ve been avoiding anything that reminds me of my old job. Office buildings, security talks, networking events near work sites—I just steer clear. And if someone starts asking about what happened that day, I usually make an excuse and leave.
At your old job, did something happen that felt life-threatening or could have seriously injured you or someone else?
I’m not sure what you mean exactly. I know I don’t like talking about that job, but I can’t say there was one particular thing like that.
Do unwanted memories of what happened at that job ever pop into your mind even when you don’t want them to?

Yes. It can happen out of nowhere—when I’m washing dishes, or if I drive past a warehouse gate. The scene just comes back so clearly. I can hear people panicking, and my chest tightens like I’m right back there.
During what happened at your old job, did you believe that you or someone else might die or be seriously hurt?
I... I don’t know. I haven’t really thought of it in those terms. I just know it was frightening, and I don’t like going back over it.
When that happened at your old job, did it seem to you that someone could be killed or seriously injured?
I’m not sure. I remember being very scared, but I can’t say for certain that I thought someone was going to be killed or seriously injured.
At that old job, was there a specific event where you thought someone might be seriously hurt or killed?
I can’t say that I remember a specific moment where I thought someone was going to be killed or badly hurt. I just remember feeling frightened and overwhelmed.
When these memories hit, does it ever feel as if the event is happening again right now?

Yes. It can come out of nowhere—I'll be washing dishes or driving past a warehouse gate, and suddenly it’s so sharp. I can hear the panic in people’s voices, my chest tightens, and for a moment it feels like I’m back there.
What happened that day at your old job?

I remember seeing a gun, and then... there’s just a blank spot. I can tell you all the mistakes they blamed me for afterward, but the confrontation right after I saw it—I can’t piece that part together, no matter how hard I try.
How long have these memories and avoidance been happening since that incident at your old job?
Since I was fired after the armed incident—about a year and seven months now.
Since that armed incident, have you been constantly on guard or easily startled?
Yes. Whenever I go into a meeting room or a restaurant, I automatically look for the exits first. I watch people’s hands, and I usually choose a seat where no one can come up behind me.
Since the armed incident, have you often felt persistent guilt, blame, or a sense that you or others can’t be trusted because of what happened?
Yes. Since then, I keep thinking you really can’t trust people to be safe. Even someone you managed or tried to help can turn around and become dangerous.
